content: The Bleed Purple Foundation is a charitable organization officially recognized under section 501(c)(3) of the IRS code. It is based in Denver, Colorado, and was established in 2005 by members of the Theta Zeta chapter of the Delta Tau Delta International Fraternity. The foundation was created in response to one of their fraternity brothers being diagnosed with stage III-B Hodgkin's Lymphoma. In a demonstration of fraternity brotherhood and unwavering solidarity, the members organized a head-shaving auction on the University of San Diego campus. This event successfully raised over $4,000 to support their brother, marking the inception of the Bleed Purple Foundation. The mission of Bleed Purple is to provide support to college students who are battling cancer. For many college students, managing financial responsibilities is already a significant challenge. Between attending classes, participating in campus organizations, completing unpaid internships, and dedicating time to late-night study sessions, it is often nearly impossible to maintain a job that can cover basic living expenses, let alone the overwhelming costs of medical treatment. Bleed Purple aims to unite the Greek community to offer assistance to college students diagnosed with cancer. The foundation's primary objective is to alleviate the financial burdens faced by these students as they navigate the challenges of their illness.
